ok,

In that case it kind of defeats the idea of using Thunderbird on the mobile if it has no advantage over the next randon email client. IMO the idea between using the same client on different device is that you are data and experience is the same. Your messages get synced, in the inbox as well as the sent folders. Your folder structure is shared. And you see the same set of emails in both clients. Now I have a situation where the desktop shows the relevant emails as spam is cleared and filters are run. While on the mobile I am just wading thru spam, many of the times legit emails just dont show up. So if I step out of my seat and check my mobile I cant even see what email I had sent while on the desktop client. So as a Thunderbird desktop user there is no advantage using the thunderbird mobile client. I could use gmail or outlook and probably get better spam capabilities and better editing features..
